bankAccounts.emptyBody: Add a bank account to import statements and create payment orders.

statements.subtitle: Import a bank statement – receipts and payments are matched to invoices automatically, you confirm.
statements.formats: camt.053 XML (all Estonian banks) or a bank CSV (Swedbank, SEB, LHV, Luminor, Coop). Transactions already imported are skipped.
statements.noBanks: Add a bank account first (Payments → Banks and cash).
statements.emptyBody: Download a camt.053 or CSV statement from your online bank and import it here.
statements.confirmedSome: Confirmed {confirmed}, {failed} lines need a manual look.
statements.deleteConfirm: Delete the statement? No payments have been created from it yet.
statements.accountHint: E.g. bank fee, tax payment, loan, owner's contribution.
statements.balanceDifference: The balance sheet doesn't balance: difference {amount}. Check that accounts are linked to report lines.
statements.comparePrevYear: Compare with the same period last year
statements.scheme2Note: An expense account's function can be set in the chart of accounts. By default, materials go to cost of sales and other operating expenses to administrative expenses.
statements.cashFlowNote: Cash flows are derived from changes in balance sheet lines; the total equals the change in cash.
statements.cashFlowDifference: The cash flow total differs from the change in cash by {amount} – check how accounts are linked to balance sheet lines.

paymentOrders.subtitle: Choose open purchase invoices and expense reports, create a pain.001 file and upload it to your online bank.
paymentOrders.nothingToPay: No open purchase invoices or expense reports.
paymentOrders.created: Payment order created, the file is downloading.
paymentOrders.noBankIban: Add an IBAN to the bank account (Payments → Banks and cash).
paymentOrders.markPaidConfirm: Mark the payment order as paid? A confirmed payment is created for each line.

cashbook.noCashBody: Add a cash desk (Payments → Banks and cash).

vatReturn.subtitle: Period {from} – {to}
vatReturn.closeConfirm: I'll post a closing entry moving output and input VAT balances to the VAT settlement account. Continue?
vatReturn.closedInfo: The period is closed with entry
vatReturn.unknownRates: Some lines use a rate the return has no line for: {rates}%. Check the VAT codes.
vatReturn.note: Calculated from confirmed documents and entries. Review before filing; the XML file can be uploaded to e-MTA.
vatReturn.partA: KMD INF part A – sales invoices
vatReturn.partB: KMD INF part B – purchase invoices
vatReturn.noInf: No partners with invoices of at least €1,000 excluding VAT in this period.

lines.l1: Supplies at the standard rate (24%, before 1 Jul 2025 22%)
lines.l3_1: Intra-community supply of goods and services to taxable persons in other member states
lines.l3_2_1: incl. sales to travellers with VAT refund
lines.l5_3: incl. passenger cars used 100% for business
lines.l5_4: incl. passenger cars partly used for business
lines.l6: Intra-community acquisition of goods and services received from EU taxable persons
lines.l7: Other acquisitions subject to reverse charge
lines.l7_1: incl. immovables, scrap metal and precious metals (VAT Act § 41¹)
lines.l9: Supplies under domestic reverse charge (VAT Act § 41¹)

docReports.emptyTitle: No confirmed invoices in this period
docReports.note: Amounts in EUR at the invoice rate; credit notes are negative.
docReports.notePurchases: Amounts in EUR at the invoice rate; non-deductible VAT is part of the cost. Expense reports aren't included.

debts.emptyBody: All invoices are paid as of this date.
debts.note: Amounts in EUR at the invoice rate. Prepayments reduce the partner balance; paid includes nettings.

recurring.listSubtitle: Repeating invoices (rent, maintenance, subscriptions) – created automatically on schedule.
recurring.newSubtitle: A template that produces an invoice every month, quarter or year. Descriptions can contain placeholders.
recurring.editSubtitle: Changes apply to future invoices; invoices already created don't change.
recurring.name: Name
recurring.nameHint: For you only – not shown to the customer.
recurring.runConfirm: Create the next invoice now (with its scheduled date)?

sendResult.noEmail: The invoice was created, but the customer has no email address – send it manually.
sendResult.emailFailed: The invoice was created, but sending the email failed.
sendResult.rateLimited: The invoice was created, but the hourly email limit is reached – send it later.
sendResult.emailNotConfigured: The invoice was created, but email sending isn't configured.

recurring.deleteConfirm: Delete recurring invoice “{name}”? Invoices already created are kept.
recurring.emptyBody: Add a template when the same invoice goes to a customer regularly.

interest.subtitle: Late interest on overdue invoices as of {date}. Periods already charged aren't counted again.
interest.emptyBody: No invoice has been paid late or remains overdue.
interest.note: Interest = unpaid amount × rate × days; the payment day still counts as late. The rate comes from the invoice (customer or company setting). Interest invoices carry no VAT.

reminders.subtitle: Payment reminders and balance statements for customers – PDF and email in the customer's language.
reminders.sendConfirmReminder: Send a payment reminder to {count} customers?
reminders.sendConfirmStatement: Send a balance statement to {count} customers?
reminders.emptyBody: Change the date or the days limit.
reminders.textHint: Email text can be changed in Settings → Invoice settings.
reminders.logEmpty: No reminders or statements sent yet.

consolidated.subtitle: Pick quotes or orders of one customer – they become a single invoice draft.
consolidated.emptyBody: Consolidated invoices are made from quotes that haven't been invoiced yet.

statementEmail.reminderBody: According to our records, invoices totalling {total} were unpaid as of {date}. Please pay them at your earliest convenience. The list of invoices is attached. If you have already paid, please disregard this email.
statementEmail.statementBody: Please find our balance statement as of {date}: your balance with us is {total}. Kindly confirm it or let us know if your records differ. The list of invoices is attached.

statementPdf.introReminder: According to our records, the following invoices were overdue as of {date}. Please pay them at your earliest convenience.
statementPdf.introStatement: According to our accounting records, your balance as of {date} is as follows.
statementPdf.confirmText: Please confirm the balance as of {date} and return it signed to {company}.
statementPdf.disagree: We do not confirm – our balance is: __________________

viewer.label: Preview: {name}
viewer.noPreview: No preview for this file – download it.
viewer.hint: Wheel zooms · drag to move · double-click

newSubtitle.RECEIPT: Goods into stock without a purchase invoice – e.g. opening stock or own production. Rows without a unit cost use the current cost.
newSubtitle.ISSUE: Goods out of stock without a sales invoice – e.g. write-off, samples or own use.
newSubtitle.TRANSFER: Moving goods from one warehouse to another. The value doesn't change and no entry is made.
newSubtitle.COUNT: Enter the counted quantities. The difference from the book quantity is posted to the counter account.

counterHint.RECEIPT: E.g. an equity account for opening stock, or an expense account for own production.
counterHint.ISSUE: The expense account for the cost of the issued goods.
counterHint.COUNT: Expense account for shortages or income account for surpluses.

inventory.movementsSubtitle: Receipts, issues, transfers, stock counts and movements from sales and purchase invoices.
inventory.searchMovements: Search by number, description or item
inventory.emptyBody: Mark items as stock items and movements are created from purchase and sales invoices. Enter opening stock as a receipt.
inventory.countHint: Add rows yourself or fill in every item in stock and correct the counted quantities.
inventory.warehousesSubtitle: Warehouses, the value of their stock and how cost is calculated.
inventory.warehouseDeactivated: The warehouse has been used, so it was marked as not in use.
inventory.noWarehousesBody: The first warehouse, “Põhiladu”, is created with the first stock movement. Add more here if you need them.
inventory.costingBody: Cost is calculated per item across all warehouses. Changing the method or recalculating updates the cost and entries of movements in open periods; closed periods aren't changed.
inventory.costMethodConfirm: Change the costing method? The cost and entries of issues in open periods will be recalculated.
inventory.recalculated: {count, plural, =0 {Costs were already up to date.} one {Updated # movement.} other {Updated # movements.}}
inventory.noStockBody: Stock comes from purchase invoices and receipts.
inventory.warehouseValueNote: A warehouse's value is the sum of its movements. Cost is calculated across warehouses, so the unit cost in one warehouse may differ.
inventory.checkHint: A difference appears when manual entries were posted to the inventory account or a stock item on a purchase invoice went to another account. Check the account in the general ledger.
inventory.noStockItemsBody: Mark goods as stock items under Items.
inventory.noSalesTitle: No stock items sold in this period
inventory.noSalesBody: The analysis shows stock items on confirmed sales invoices.
inventory.analysisNote: Revenue comes from stock item rows on confirmed sales invoices and credit notes, in euros without VAT; cost comes from those invoices' stock movements.
